knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Product Containing an Exponential or Logarithmic Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=2\log_{2} x$ and $v(x)=\ln x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(2\log_{2} x)^{′}\ln x+2\log_{2} x(\ln x)^{′} \\  & =(\frac{2}{x \ln{\left(2 \right)}})(\ln x)+(2\log_{2} x)(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{2\log_{2} x}{x} + \frac{2\ln x}{x\ln 2}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=x^{-4}$ and $v(x)=\log_{2} x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(x^{-4})^{′}\log_{2} x+x^{-4}(\log_{2} x)^{′} \\  & =(- \frac{4}{x^{5}})(\log_{2} x)+(x^{-4})(\frac{1}{x \ln{\left(2 \right)}}) \\  & =x^{-5}(-4\log_{2} x + \frac{1}{\ln 2})\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)={5}^{x}$ and $v(x)=\sin (x).$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{'}(x) & ={({5}^{x})}^{'}\sin (x)+{5}^{x}{(\sin (x))}^{'} \\  & =({5}^{x}\ln (5))\sin (x)+{5}^{x}(\cos (x)) \\  & ={5}^{x}\ln (5)\sin (x)+{5}^{x}\cos (x)\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)={x}^{2}$ and $v(x)={e}^{2x}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{'}(x) & =({x}^{2})^{'}{e}^{2x}+{x}^{2}({e}^{2x})^{'} \\  & =(2x)({e}^{2x})+({x}^{2})(2{e}^{2x}) \\  & =2x{e}^{2x}+2{x}^{2}{e}^{2x}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=x$ and $v(x)={2}^{x}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =(x)^{′}\cdot {2}^{x}+x\cdot ({2}^{x})^{′} \\  & ={2}^{x}+(x)(\ln  2\cdot {2}^{x}) \\  & ={2}^{x}+x\ln  2\cdot {2}^{x} \\  & =(1+x\ln  2){2}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(\cos  x)}^{′}\log _{2} x+\cos  x{(\log _{2} x)}^{′} \\  & =(-\sin  x)(\log _{2} x)+(\cos  x)(\frac{1}{x\ln  2}) \\  & =\frac{\cos  x}{x\ln  2}-\sin  x\log _{2} x\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
